account:
Today has seemed quiet so far. During my scheduled morning market walk, several townsfolk told me they had no news. I bought a fresh loaf for lunch and asked freight about the docks and warehouse, but I heard no reply. I have seen no clear sign of trouble or unusual activity.

The only unresolved matter is my fifteen-hundred tea appointment, listed simply as tea with 'the neighbour, dockside cottage, east bank.' Neither the host's name nor the exact cottage was recorded. The secretary took the appointment book to review it and said she would visit the east-bank cottages to identify the host before fifteen hundred. As far as I know, this is ordinary work to clarify an incomplete invitation, not evidence of anything more unusual. I have not yet received her confirmation.

I am now home at noon for my scheduled lunch. My next business is town accounts at the office at thirteen hundred, followed by the tea visit, office time at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen hundred.
